title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: Charges Counted Against a Remittance
content:
## Clause

When a remittance covering the charges of a Dangerous Goods Acceptance file is applied, the charges it is measured against are rebuilt from the acceptance's account. On the charge side they take in, over the acceptance's entire life:

| Group | Entries included |
|---|---|
| Charges raised at approval and loading | every administration-fee entry, every hazardous-cargo surcharge entry and every marine-pollutant surcharge entry |
| Fees | every late declaration fee, every amendment fee and re-review fee, and every withdrawal fee |
| Penalties | every misdeclaration penalty and every inspection cost recovery |

## Principle: the figure must be complete

These charges are meant to stand for what the acceptance truly owes. Because they are rebuilt entry by entry from the account, they do so only when the account itself is complete. For goods that have been loaded, the charges that loading brings due — the hazardous-cargo surcharge and, for goods marked marine pollutant, the marine-pollutant surcharge — are part of what the acceptance owes. A figure rebuilt from an account on which such a charge is missing understates the debt, is not the figure this rule means, and cannot be the basis of the amount a remittance is applied at.

## Worked case (invented amounts)

An acceptance shows an administration fee of 80.00, a hazardous-cargo surcharge of 1227.60 and an amendment fee of 130.00. The charge side totals 1437.60. A withdrawal fee or penalty, had there been one, would be counted in the same way.

## Point of judgement

**Does a re-review fee belong on the charge side?** Yes; it is counted together with the amendment fees.
